caption: The drawing features a single, vertically-oriented wooden door positioned centrally against a plain, light beige or off-white background. The door is narrow and rectangular, with a slightly darker wooden frame around its edges. In the upper portion of the door, there is a square inset panel, attached with visible rivets or nails at the corners. The texture of the door is depicted with fine lines and patterns to suggest wood grain, showing various knots and natural imperfections. Several ornate, metallic-looking fittings or bosses are attached to the door in two vertical rows—mostly small, round, and dark-colored, with a few larger decorative elements in the same dark tone. There are a couple of small, white irregular patches on the door surface, possibly indicating damage or wear. No other objects or decorative elements are present in the composition, and the door occupies most of the vertical space on the page. In the bottom right corner of the image, there is a small, legible printed inscription: “HAVIC [or HAVIE?] HANSEN.”
title: Copper-studded Door (One of a Pair)
